**No.** The story is a quiet, atmospheric vignette rather than one built on real turns. The crossing goes exactly as Ilse predicts: the fog, the seemingly abnormal noise ("Klang immer so"), and the boy's "Da ist ja wirklich Land" all resolve into routine and confirm expectations rather than overturning them.

The only real shift is the call from Jonas, which Ilse lets ring out. It fits the faint hints that something weighs on her ("An solchen Morgen half es, sich an die kleinen Dinge zu halten"). But it is too slight and undeveloped to work as a surprising twist. It is more an open, suggestive ending than a turn that reframes what came before.
